doc.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998

chapter: Songs, singers and the state of jazz
title: Songs she has sung all her career
summary: She still sings "The Masquerade Is Over," "Ghost of a Chance" and "Don't Go To Strangers."

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Can you think of a tune or tunes that you’ve been singing almost from the start of your career that you still do?
I don’t sing that anymore. I think it was “The Masquerade is Over.” I still do that sometimes, or “Ghost of a Chance.” Although it seems like I’ve been singing some of these songs all my life.
Do you still do “Don’t Go To Strangers?”
“Don’t Go To Stranger,” oh yes. They still ask for that. And I say oh God. But you know I was so happy to get that song that it pleases me when I do it because I would still be—
